findings.evidence: The new RFC 8291 Appendix A end-to-end test forces the worker's output to match the fixed vector by globally spying on crypto.getRandomValues (mockImplementationOnce, relies on the salt being the first random draw), crypto.subtle.generateKey (ECDH only) and JSON.stringify (returns the RFC plaintext for any object with link_path and title). Decrypting the RFC body and the byte-for-byte equality of the worker body both pass on the Target.
findings.impact: The vector check is valuable, but it is coupled to implementation details: a future worker change that draws another random value before the salt, calls JSON.stringify differently, or generates a second ECDH key would break or silently weaken the test without any crypto regression. Test-only, no production effect.
findings.recommendation: Optional follow-up: let handleSendNotificationsRequest (or a thin encrypt helper) accept injectable salt, ephemeral key pair and payload so the vector test needs no global spies, and keep the direct decryptWebPushPayload vector assertion as is. Not blocking for merge.
